newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Pac in share placement to expand.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Pac in share placement to expand.

text.p: Container leasing and terminal operating firm COSCO Pacific Ltd said on Monday it raised HK$1.199 billion for group expansion through an exercise of share placement by its China-owned parent COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd.

The parent on Monday placed 120 million existing COSCO Pacific shares at HK$9.95 each to international investors, and will subscribe for the same number of new shares at the same price on April 14 contingent on the approval of COSCO Pacific shareholders, director and general manager Kelvin Wong told a news conference.
The placement price represents a five percent discount to the last closing share price of HK$10.50 on Friday. Trading in the stock was suspended on Monday at the firm's own request.
Of the proceeds from the placement, HK$455 million will be used to buy stakes in four Chinese ports from COSCO (Hong Kong).
They are a half stake in Qingdao Terminal, a 51 percent stake in Zhangjiagang Terminal, a 10 percent stake in Shanghai Terminal and a five percent stake in Yantian Terminal.

Wong said the price represented a 31 percent discount to the stakes' net asset value of HK$655 million, a 52 percent discount to their appraised value of HK$954 million, and 10 times their 1996 net earnings of HK$45.4 million.
The deal would strengthen the listed firm's net assets and earnings per share, he said.
The four ports had a total throughput of 2.2 million TEU (20-foot equivalent units) in 1996, expected to reach 4.6 million TEU by 2000, the firm said.

Another HK$250 million from the placement proceeds will be used to expand COSCO Pacific's Chinese terminals and container manufacturing plants, and another HK$494 million will be used to buy container terminals in Asia Pacific, the firm said.
But company officials declined to name any possible target.
The placement, underwritten by BZW Asia Ltd and Salomon Brothers, reduced the parent's stake in the listed firm to 55 percent from 62 percent, Wong said.
But its shareholding will be raised to slightly below 59 percent after the subscription of new shares, he said.
COSCO Pacific, which claims to be the fifth largest container leasing company worldwide, post a 63.3 percent growth in net profit to HK$585.9 million for 1996.

It attributed the rise to growth in container leasing and improvement in profit margin at Hong Kong's Container Terminal Eight (East) which is run and managed by a joint venture held 50 percent by the group.
Its container fleet rose 17.9 percent to 343,245 TEU, and the number of container leasing clients rose to 38 as at the end of 1996 from 20 a year earlier.
COSCO (Hong Kong) is considering investing in container terminals in the Far East, including Malaysia and Australia, the parent group's executive vice chairman Zhang Dachun said.
